_comment: Which local tests run on GitHub Actions, and in which order they are turned on.  Enabling more is a reviewed edit of this file.
The single workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml compiles once per platform ('build' job), uploads the workspace, then runs every
(platform, job) pair that has an enabled entry as its own 'test' job (in parallel, each on a fresh machine, so jobs cannot interfere through

ports, config directories or temp files; the lanes of one job - see 'job' below - and the entries of one lane run one after another on that machine). Test assemblies are prebuilt; some integration journeys restore temporary fixture projects using the populated package cache.
throughBatch: entries whose batch is greater than this are planned but not run.  workflow_dispatch can override it.

focus: true runs only the 'observe' entries on each platform (a 'required' one has passed twice in a row), which saves runner time while many entries still fail; a lane left with no entry is not scheduled.  workflow_dispatch with full=true runs everything once; set focus to false to return to full runs.
Per platform an entry is 'observe' (runs; a failure is reported as a warning and does not fail the job), 'required' (a failure fails
the job) or 'excluded' (does not run; 'reason' says why).  A platform missing from an entry is excluded.  A new batch starts as 'observe';
promote it to 'required' after it has been green on that platform for several runs.

A device journey (a real Android emulator or an iOS Simulator) may run only in a lane that declares its class under 'deviceClasses' together with the OS family whose runner hosts the device: 'macos' for the iOS Simulator, which is a native macOS process, and 'linux' for the Android emulator, which needs KVM. .github/ci/tests/verify-no-device-journeys.ps1 fails the plan job for any entry that runs a device class from a lane that does not declare it, and for a declared lane whose runner is not of that family. Every other entry stays off devices; those journeys run by hand on a developer machine.
kind: xunit-exe = dotnet <target> [args] (an xUnit v3 test assembly, run directly); msbuild = dotnet msbuild <target> -t:Build.
'project' is built once in the build job (distinct projects only).  'measuredSeconds' is the last measured duration; keep it current when promoting a batch.

'buildFirst' projects are built before everything else on every platform that builds: the host's build writes the host-assembly manifest that lets every add-in trim what the host already ships (without it each add-in carries ~550 MB of copy-local dependencies and AddIns reaches 13 GB); tests/OpenDevelop.IntegrationTests/TESTING.md says the same: build the application first.

'buildArgs' are extra dotnet build arguments for the entry's 'project'; entries that share a project must agree on them.  The integration project is built with -p:BuildIntegrationFixtures=false because its fixture target builds every fixture inside one MSBuild process (Uno.Sdk 6.6.42 then clashes with the already resolved 6.5.31, MSB4240); a lane that needs a fixture lists that fixture's own csproj as an entry 'project' so it builds in its own process.

A lane with 'needsNuGetCache' also downloads the build job's NuGet package cache: the IDE host resolves its LibreWPF assemblies from the global packages folder at run time, so a lane that starts the IDE (the integration lanes) needs it; the unit lane does not.

'buildLast' projects are built after everything else, with their own 'args' ('{rid}' is the platform's 'rid').  The host is built last with '--runtime <rid> -p:AppendRuntimeIdentifierToOutputPath=false', the recipe terminal-cross-platform.yml uses (it builds the Terminal add-in that way, which builds the host project it references as that RID into the same folder) and whose IDE does start on the Windows runner.  Measured on the runner without it: the host's OpenDevelop.deps.json is 166 libraries without a 'PresentationFramework/11.0.0.0' reference entry from the very first host build on, whatever is built afterwards in the default way (a macOS build has 193, with 28 'reference' entries for the LibreWPF assemblies), and the IDE dies at start-up with a FileNotFoundException for PresentationFramework 11.0.0.0.  The build summary records the host deps.json after every build, so the run shows what the RID-specific build changes.

A lane definition holds 'timeoutMinutes', optionally 'needsNuGetCache' (the IDE host resolves its LibreWPF assemblies from the global packages folder at run time), 'needsGtk' for native GTK dependencies, and 'entryTimeoutMinutes' (an entry's default budget), and 'job': lanes of one platform that name the same job run one after another in ONE CI job, so the platform's archive is downloaded and unpacked once (the quick lanes - unit, integration-stable, integration-unstable - are job 'fast'; the long designer lane is its own job and runs in parallel); a job's timeout is the sum of its lanes' timeouts plus 30 minutes of preparation headroom.  A lane may also name 'runner' (its job runs on that image instead of the platform's, which is how the iOS Simulator lane gets Xcode 27) and 'deviceClasses' (the device journeys it may run, with the OS family that hosts the device - see the entry above). A platform may also name 'singleJob' to run all of its lanes in one job: macOS does ('macos'), because a macOS runner image is the scarce resource and one acquisition then finishes every lane instead of one queue entry per job. A lane that names 'standalone' stays out of that merge and keeps its own job: mobile-ios does, because the Simulator lane needs the xcode-27 image, its SDK 11 and a booted simulator, which must not share the machine that runs the other macOS lanes.

'additionalProjects' declares fixture projects needed by an enabled entry; optional platforms refer to the build platform, so Windows ARM64 prerequisites belong to windows-x64 when it supplies the shared archive.

Profiler and Terminal are entries here; their own workflows (profiler.yml, terminal-cross-platform.yml) were deleted when they were folded in. Windows ARM64 and macOS ARM64 start as observed Terminal journeys and are promoted after repeated green runs.

platformNotes.macos-arm64: dist.macos.sh ships an osx-arm64-only payload, so this platform builds for itself and its archive drops the Windows RID trees the package never contains. 'singleJob': 'macos' puts the platform's non-standalone lanes (unit, integration-stable, integration-unstable, integration-designer) in one job, because a macOS runner is the scarce resource: one acquisition then finishes them instead of two jobs queueing separately. mobile-ios is 'standalone' and keeps its own job on xcode-27, because its SDK 11, iOS workload and booted simulator must not share the machine with the GUI lanes; run 42362589732 lost that merged job with 'runner lost communication' while the designer lane ran, taking the whole macOS result with it.
platformNotes.windows-x64: Every unit and integration entry is required here since 2026-10-27 (base-tests and xamldom-tests-microsoftwpf were the last unit entries promoted), so focus mode schedules no Windows x64 job beyond the build, which windows-arm64 still needs.
platformNotes.windows-arm64: Runs the native Windows ARM64 Terminal journey against the same unified Windows payload the x64 lane tests: dist.windows.bat ships one package with runtimes/ plus per-RID win-x64/win-arm64 folders and both launchers, so 'buildFrom': 'windows-x64' keeps a single compile for both lanes.
platformNotes.linux-x64: Enabled on 2026-11-02 with the unit suites (Profiler among them, which profiler.yml once ran on ubuntu-latest) and the workbench and DevFlow journeys, all 'observe'. The IDE entries run under xvfb-run with Mesa's software Vulkan driver (install-linux-prerequisites.sh); promote per the usual two green runs.
platformNotes.linux-arm64: Same entries and rules as linux-x64, on the native ubuntu-24.04-arm runner: dist.linux.sh ships one archive per Linux architecture, so each builds for itself.

unit.note: The unit suites, run like every other lane from the archive of their platform's build, first in its platform's job ('fast' on Windows and Linux; macOS merges every lane into one job); Windows ARM64 ('buildFrom': 'windows-x64') runs the x64 build it ships. An entry gets 10 minutes, so one that hangs (for example a test whose child application cannot open a window) cannot use up the whole lane; the longest measured entry took about a minute (base-tests 61-64 s, profiler-tests 43-44 s on the Linux unit jobs of run 41393644443), and the job timeout (the lanes' timeouts plus 30 minutes) leaves room for unpacking the archive and restoring the package cache.

integration-stable.note: Entries that passed on every hosted run in which the IDE started (runs 40431285339 through 40461019311): workbench, the stable core journeys, code coverage and the ARM64 unit suites, sharing one preparation. Windows x64 measured about 28 minutes of tests plus ~15 minutes of preparation. Its entries are required on macOS ARM64 and Windows x64 after each passed on the last two hosted runs that completed it there; on Windows ARM64 they are required too, after passing on runs 40444468212, 40461019311 and 40470967407. In focus mode the lane has no entry left and is not scheduled. new-project-dialog-macos joined later: it failed on the hosted runner until cc569fd5a8 and moved here after passing runs 40606824351 and 40615707034.

integration-designer.note: All designer journeys (LibreWPF, LibreWinForms, MewUI, GTK) in one lane. Entries in a lane run serially, so the LibreWPF journeys that edit src/Samples still never share the sample with a concurrent test. Windows: ~15 minutes preparation, 3.5 minutes GTK install, 24-28 minutes of LibreWPF editing. macOS runs this lane in the merged 'macos' job with the platform's unit and integration lanes, after they finish.

mobile-ios.note: The iOS Simulator debugging journey (Debugger.AddIn's IosSimulatorProjectBehavior) on the xcode-27 image: an iOS Simulator is a native macOS process, so no nested virtualisation is involved, but the .NET 11 iOS workload set pins Microsoft.NET.Sdk.iOS 27.0.12212-net11-rc.2, which accepts only Xcode 27.0. The image's default is Xcode 27.1, so the job selects the 27.0 that ships beside it (xcode-select /Applications/Xcode_27.app), installs the SDK 11 and its ios workload into ~/.dotnet and boots one iPhone simulator; the journey registers that SDK through od.sdk.add-custom-root and attaches SharpDbg to the app it installs with simctl. The lane is 'standalone', so it keeps its own job on xcode-27 and the other macOS lanes never install the workload or boot a simulator. allowAllFailures is the bootstrap exception (a lane whose only entry failed fails the lane): drop it and promote the entry to required after two green runs.

mobile-android.note: The Android debugging journey (Debugger.AddIn's AndroidDebugProjectBehavior) against a headless emulator on the hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner, the only runner image family with KVM (macOS arm64 and ubuntu-24.04-arm have no nested virtualisation). The job enables /dev/kvm, installs the android workload next to the SDK 11 it puts in ~/.dotnet, and boots one google_apis x86_64 AVD, whose ABI the archive's AddIns/Debugger/android/x86_64 agent covers. allowAllFailures is the bootstrap exception (a lane whose only entry failed fails the lane): drop it and promote the entry to required after two green runs.

integration-unstable.note: Entries with known hosted failures or under investigation: macOS Terminal pointer input and debugger-journeys on Windows ARM64 (one flaky stop, fixed in c7497292df, awaiting a second green run). base-tests-arm, add-reference-journey and debugger-feature-journeys are required on every platform since 2026-10-28 but stay here for now: moving them into integration-stable would lengthen a lane with a 55-minute timeout that nobody has re-measured, and a full run is not due yet. Plan order runs Hot Reload last so a hang there does not hide the others. The lane is defined last so that, in the merged macOS job, its pointer journeys run after the designer and Simulator lanes: a leftover IDE window from an observe entry must not sit in front of a designer drag.

buildLast.note: macOS and Linux are single-architecture payloads (dist.macos.sh, dist.linux.sh), so building the add-in for that RID is harmless and stages the native Terminal assets the lanes use. On Windows the unified payload already carries runtimes/win-x64 and win-arm64, so a RID build is what used to strip the host folder - the build guard rejects it there.
Publish the Windows host after the RID-specific Terminal build restores its mutable payload outputs.

entries.note: Microsoft's XamlReader is loaded on its own STA thread with a 20-second deadline; on a cold runner the first cases can exceed it and report HANG. One case failed that way on 2026-10-25 while the other 96 passed.

entries.reason: Observed while validating the all-platform LibGhostty.Net 1.0.2 package; promote after repeated green runs.

entries.note: First batch-4 cross-platform integration entry. Opens an isolated Razor SDK project and asserts HTML, CSS, JavaScript and C# highlighting through the running IDE. Measured locally on macOS ARM64: 1 test in 28 seconds; keep observe until repeated runner results are stable.

macOS ARM64: 7 passed and the Windows-only SDK download case skipped. On the hosted runner it failed until cc569fd5a8 (templates from the runtime-matching SDK folder only), then passed runs 40606824351 and 40615707034.
Covers template dialogs and project creation. The SDK-selection theory is excluded on Windows because one data row installs an SDK over the network; schedule it separately with its own time budget.

Issue #24: the real Project Browser context menu on a project node (Rename, Delete, Remove present and enabled), then rename and delete on a copy of SlnxFixture - the .csproj, the .slnx entry and a rebuild under the new name. Starts as observe.

Issue #23: OD_IGNORE_DOTNET_SDKS simulates a machine with no .NET SDK, so the IDE must report it at startup and leave. One fact checks the exit code and the log; the other finds the WPF dialog through EnumWindows, posts WM_CLOSE and requires the same exit, which is why it runs on Windows only. Starts as observe: promote after two green hosted runs.

Exercises the modal Add Reference dialog with native clicks and verifies project and assembly references. It passes on hosted macOS ARM64 and Windows x64; on Windows ARM64 the dialog never got native focus because the image sits on the first-logon privacy page; the Prepare the Windows desktop step (32fd2eda79) clears it, and it then passed runs 40662664664 and 40671568295 there.
Protects integration fixture port ownership and cleanup on initialization failure.
Full profiler journeys, including capture isolation, web service, heap, launch and test-host profiling. macOS ARM64 locally passed 21 cases with the Windows WPF case skipped in 107 seconds.

30 LibreWPF designer editing journeys. Hosted Windows x64 (1389 s) and ARM64 (1569 s) passed all 30 in runs 40595645276 and 40606824351; hosted macOS ARM64 still fails CtrlPointerGestures_DistinguishClickCollapseFromGroupDrag.
Exercises LibreWinForms image-list editing and undo.
Uses the LibreWPF sample on macOS; the same method selects the Microsoft WPF backend on Windows and is not enabled there without its host.
Ten MewUI designer journeys passed locally on macOS ARM64 in 55 seconds. Each case restores a temporary fixture; building the fixture primes the NuGet cache.

Twelve GTK host, native preview, editing, recovery and libadwaita journeys passed locally on macOS ARM64 in 66 seconds. Hosted Windows x64 passed all twelve on runs 40495471973 and 40524161593; Windows ARM64 failed the toolbox drag onto the native surface until the desktop preparation step (32fd2eda79), then passed all twelve in runs 40662664664 and 40671568295. Hosted macOS still fails the toolbox drag and the real pads case.

Nested GTK selection, property editing, insertion, undo and save passed locally on macOS ARM64 in 20 seconds. It shares GtkDesignerFixture with the other GTK entries; its document is ui/mainWindow.ui.
Includes native-host and per-architecture journeys; skips describe missing compatible runtimes or architectures.

Exercises breakpoint inspection, stepping, restart and attaching to an independently started process. On the hosted macOS runner every attach hung in ICorDebug.DebugActiveProcess until ci.yml granted system.privilege.taskport (a24f882e56); with it, both debugger entries passed runs 40582707365 and 40595645276. On Windows ARM64 one case failed until e2dc739e95 mapped the x64 build job's source paths onto the ARM64 workspace; it then passed runs 40662664664 and 40671568295.
Exercises real test discovery, coverage collection and editor markers using prebuilt test fixtures.
Exercises real WPF application and class-library Hot Reload journeys; Microsoft WPF variants run only on Windows. macOS ARM64 locally passed four journeys with two Windows-only skips.

First batch-4 designer-host entry. Opens the LibreWPF designer, waits until its out-of-process host loads the project assembly, then rebuilds and rejects file-lock diagnostics. Measured locally on macOS ARM64: 1 test in 47 seconds; keep observe until repeated runner results are stable.

Builds a net11.0-ios app with the SDK 11 the lane installed, installs and launches it stopped through simctl, attaches SharpDbg with the app's own retargeted mscordbi, and stops at a breakpoint in FinishedLaunching. The journey skips when no iPhone simulator or SDK 11 with the iOS workload exists, and xUnit reports a skip as a passing total, so read the entry's own result rather than the lane's colour.

Builds a net11.0-android app with the SDK 11 the lane installed, deploys it to the headless emulator through adb, stops at a breakpoint, steps, evaluates and checks that the session leaves no debug-app setting or adb forward behind; then repeats the session. The journey skips when adb or exactly one connected device is missing, and xUnit reports a skip as a passing total, so read the entry's own result rather than the lane's colour.
